Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Work & responsibility · Money, work & business

employment noun

having paid work

also paid work, be in employment, find employment, a living, livelihood, occupation

classical

Plaut. Rud. 2.1.2: pauperēs hominēs, quibus nec quaestus est (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 309: employment (occupation), quaestus

quaestus, quaestūs m.

noun, fourth declension

a living, paid work, a way of earning

Literally gain, profit: the work one lives by, seen as what it earns. It can be any trade, decent or not (quaestuī habēre, to make money out of something), so it is not a word of praise. For the trade as a skill, see trade (artificium); for a single piece of work or a job to be done, see job (opus).

Other words

  • opus, operis n. — work to do

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 335: job (piece of work), opus

    Work as a task, not as a livelihood: opus nōn habet, he has nothing to do. See job.

Examples

  • pauperēs hominēs, quibus nec quaestus est

    poor men, who have no livingPlaut. Rud. 2.1.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • Quaestum nōndum invēnit.

    He hasn’t found work yet.composed

See also job, trade, employ, unemployment, earn, career.

SourcesLewis & Short: quaestus · Lewis & Short: opus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 309, 335, checked against the searchable text of the book.
